description: Add a separately licensed mastery sequence connecting simulation to convergence in probability.
Qualify existence and almost-everywhere uniqueness of regular conditional distributions.
Preserve donor seeds, retain signed error, and emit a canonical CSV result table.
Use R, the domain of the composed operator, in the existence qualification.
Use the beta density's (1-x) second factor.
Integrate a T-valued conditional distribution over T.
Use the defined expectation macro in the conditional second moment.
Use y in the second matrix factor and U as the product kernel's target space.
Sum the right operator over the target index set T.
Introduce correctly typed S-domain functions for the measure identities.
Use an S-domain function in the measure-addition identity.
Use the S-domain functions in the integral additivity identity.
Quantify the second doubly stochastic condition over the target space T.
Remove the duplicated empty integral in the exponential-kernel product.
Use S as the domain of an invariant function for an endokernel on S.
Require an endokernel so the invariant-measure and invariant-function equalities are typed.
Use T in both integrals of the kernel-function proof.
Integrate the kernel function over the target space T.
Use the target sigma-algebra in the kernel measurability argument.
Use the integration variable y in the composed-kernel proof.
Put the stopping and success parameters before the observation n.
Use the positive-integer stopping parameter space for the negative binomial family.
Restore the one-half factor in the general normal density exponent.
Keep the parameter first and observation second in the normal kernel.
Restrict density powers to positive n; the identity kernel at n=0 has no Lebesgue density.
Use x consistently as the output variable in the squared normal kernel.
Restore the missing equality sign in the normal-mixture density calculation.
Place Kf in the bounded-function space on its actual domain S.
State the valid norm inequality for an arbitrary bounded function.
State the correct left action for g(r)=r under the Poisson family.
Evaluate the gamma integral as n+1 rather than n.
Do not call the positive-measure cone a real vector space.
Remove the extra closing parenthesis in the measure-space reference.
Supply the state argument in the probability-kernel product calculation.
Use rho, the target reference measure, in the product-density conclusion.
Integrate the right action of a kernel over its target space T.
Use j, rather than the unrelated i, as the index of the disjoint family.
Rewrite the upstream broken #tai1 reference to its intended limsup/liminf result #tai12 in the built reader only.
